Title: Commas, semicolons, and other separators
Detail_lesson: This detail field contains commas, several of them, plus a trailing clause that also has one, deliberately.
CustomInstruction: Answer in one sentence, using at least one comma, so the round-trip through the parser is visible in the rendered output.

Title: The word "quoted" appears here
Detail_lesson: A detail field that quotes a colleague directly: she said "ship the smaller thing first" and the room agreed.
CustomInstruction: Reply with a short quotation in double quotes, so the escaping behaviour is visible end to end.

Title: Cafe culture: resume, naive, facade
Detail_lesson: Accents and non-Latin characters in a body field: cafe becomes café, resume becomes résumé, naive becomes naïve. Also Straße, Ångström, Ø, ß, 日本語, and a mathematical minus sign −.
CustomInstruction: Answer using at least one accented character, for example naïve or café, to confirm UTF-8 survives storage and display.

Title: Only the required fields are populated

This title is deliberately far longer than any real prompt should ever be, because the point of this row is to find out what the importer, the database write, the host projector view and the player list all do when a single Title field runs well past three hundred characters without any line break to help them out
Detail_lesson: A long title should still import cleanly even though it would be unreadable on a projector.
CustomInstruction: Do not answer this one seriously - it exists to check truncation, wrapping and column width behaviour in every view that renders a Title.

Title: A detail field containing a line break
Detail_lesson:
First line of the detail field.
Second line of the same field, after an embedded newline inside the quoted value.
CustomInstruction: Confirm the second line survived the import, then answer in a single line.

Title: Commas, "quotes" and accents together
Detail_lesson: One field, three hazards: a comma, an escaped "quotation", and an accented word like Ångström - all in the same value.
CustomInstruction: Answer with a phrase that itself contains a comma, a "quoted" fragment, and one accented character.
